name: Livorno
title: Livorno Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Ro-Ro & Ferry UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Livorno for ro-ro ships, ferries, car carriers, container ships and tankers: hull, deck and piping readings, plus pre-docking.
h1: Hull Thickness Measurement in Livorno for Ro-Ro Ships, Ferries and Car Carriers
intro: Livorno is the main Tuscan port and one of the busiest ro-ro harbours in the Mediterranean, with ferry lines to the islands and Spain, car carriers, containers, forest products and an oil terminal. Many of its ships are on regular loops, so work can be repeated and planned. Atlantis NDT sends technicians from India to the ship and arranges the readings around her turnaround.

highlights.h: Ro-ro decks and ramps on regular loops
highlights.p: Livorno handles a large flow of ro-ro and ro-pax ships. Vehicle decks, ramps, stern doors and ballast spaces can be gauged between loading cycles, and repeated on later calls to follow wastage.
New vehicles and heavy rolling cargo pass over the quays. Car decks on pure car and truck carriers, with their lightweight steel and moving ramps, are a common gauging target.
Tankers calling at the oil facilities can have deck structure, deck piping and released ballast tanks measured during the call, giving owners data ahead of a vetting inspection or a sale.

port.h: The Port of Livorno: ro-ro lines, vehicle trades and an old harbour
p: Livorno lies on the Ligurian Sea coast of Tuscany, a short distance south of Pisa, and is the lead port of the Northern Tyrrhenian Sea port system, which also covers Piombino and the Elba ports. The harbour is large and layered: an old Medici port near the city, an outer harbour protected by long breakwaters, the Darsena Toscana container basin and a number of ro-ro and multipurpose berths. Livorno is Tuscany's gateway for cargo and a significant European port for ro-ro and vehicle traffic.

The traffic mix is broad. Ro-pax and ro-ro ships connect Livorno with Sardinia, Corsica, Sicily and Spain, often on overnight schedules. Pure car and truck carriers load and discharge large numbers of vehicles, and forest products, steel and general cargo move through the multipurpose berths. Container ships work the Darsena Toscana, and tankers call at the oil facilities serving the refinery and storage areas to the north of the port. Cruise ships use the passenger quays for visits to Pisa and Florence, and a yard sector in the old harbour supports repair work and yacht construction.

Livorno offers more planning room than most ro-ro ports, because ships on regular loops spend predictable hours alongside, and because the port has repair capacity of its own. That makes staged gauging realistic: one block of spaces on the first call, another on the next, with the readings merged into a single report. Open-coast weather is the main hazard. A strong libeccio can bring a swell into the outer harbour and the roadstead, and wind can slow cargo and launch operations. Large ships may wait offshore for a berth, and those waits can be used for condition gauging at the anchorage, subject to sea state.

facilities.h: Ro-ro berths, repair yards and anchorage for gauging at Livorno
p: Most gauging in Livorno is carried out alongside. On ro-ro ships, vehicle decks, ramps, internal ramps, stern and side doors and the voids below are the usual targets, with the crew agreeing which decks can be cleared for access. On car carriers, the lightweight decks and their supports are measured, and ballast tanks released by the officers can be done during the same call. Container ships at the Darsena Toscana allow a defined block of work in ballast tanks, hatch covers and piping while cargo handling continues.

The old harbour area has repair berths and graving docks used for mid-sized ships, as well as yards that build and refit yachts, and a ship planning a docking can be gauged afloat in advance, with a plan for the dock. Tankers at the oil berths are limited by cargo operations and permits, and cargo tank interiors need gas-free certification, so full cargo tank gauging is better in a yard stay. Ships waiting in the roadstead are reached by launch through the agent, and the technicians travel with their own gauges and crack detection kit, so no shore equipment is required.
list: Ro-ro and ro-pax berths: vehicle deck, ramp, stern door and ballast tank gauging between loading cycles
Car carrier quays: car deck plating, supports, ramps and ballast tank readings during vehicle handling
Darsena Toscana container terminal: ballast tank, hatch cover and piping gauging within the cargo window
Oil berths: deck, deck piping and released ballast tank gauging on tankers during discharge
Repair berths and docks in the old harbour: afloat or in-dock gauging ahead of and during steel renewal
Roadstead off Livorno: pre-purchase and charter condition gauging by launch, subject to swell

context.h: Tuscan trades, port state control and the ro-ro fleet
p: Italy is a Paris MoU state, and port state control at Livorno is carried out by the Guardia Costiera, the Italian Coast Guard, through the local Capitaneria di Porto. Ro-ro and ro-pax ships get close attention, and visible wastage on vehicle decks, ramps or door seatings is a common source of deficiencies. The Mediterranean SOx emission control area applies here, so ferries and larger ships run compliant fuel or scrubbers, and scrubber piping becomes an inspection item on regular loops.

The ro-ro and car carrier fleet includes many older ships, and owners weigh refits against replacement as EU carbon rules bite. Shipping has been inside the EU Emissions Trading System since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime has applied from 2025. A recent gauging record helps an owner decide, and helps a buyer see what steel work lies ahead. Ships calling at EU ports are also expected to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the Ship Recycling Regulation. We confirm with each client whether readings are intended for a surveyor, for an owner's own decision, for a charterer or for a sale, because the report format follows that purpose.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Livorno
jobs.p: Livorno requests tend to come from ferry and ro-ro operators, car carrier managers and tanker owners. Many ships return to the same berth, so staged programmes are common. We settle scope, spaces and report format with the superintendent before the team travels, and plan around the loading schedule. Typical requests include:
list: Vehicle deck, ramp and stern door gauging on a ro-pax ferry between rotations, ahead of a winter docking.
Car deck and ballast tank gauging on a pure car and truck carrier, mapped against the previous special survey.
Scrubber overboard piping and sea-water line readings on a ferry across several consecutive calls to trend wall loss.
Deck piping and released ballast tank gauging on a product tanker at the oil berths ahead of a vetting inspection.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a multipurpose ship in the roadstead, limited to spaces the crew can make safe.

logistics: Pisa Galileo Galilei Airport is the nearest airport to Livorno and is linked to the city by road and rail, with Florence and Genoa as alternatives for longer-haul connections. Technicians travelling from India normally connect through a European or Gulf hub. Italy is part of the Schengen area, so Schengen visas are needed and dates are fixed once they are issued. The ship's agent arranges ISPS passes, quay access and any launch for ships waiting offshore.
vessels: Forest product and general cargo ships

faqs.q: Can a ro-pax ferry be gauged between sailings at Livorno?
faqs.a: Yes. Between rotations we measure vehicle decks, ramps, doors and the tanks and voids the crew can open. Where a ferry returns to the same berth regularly, a larger scope is split across several calls and compiled into one report for the surveyor or the owner.

faqs.q: What is gauged on a car carrier?
faqs.a: The lightweight car decks and their supports, ramps, ballast tanks and deck piping. Moving ramps and salt-laden decks wear in specific ways, so we agree with the superintendent which decks can be cleared and take readings in a grid that can be compared at the next survey.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Livorno for a docking survey?
faqs.a: The old harbour has repair berths and docks that suit mid-sized ships, while larger ships often go to yards elsewhere on the Mediterranean. Whichever the owner chooses, afloat gauging beforehand gives the yard a steel estimate, and our technicians can join the docking to finish the survey.

faqs.q: Can gauging be done on a ship waiting offshore?
faqs.a: Yes, when the sea allows. A launch from the agent takes the technicians to the ship, and a libeccio swell can stop boarding. We plan a spare day, and if the ship is due to berth we may move the work alongside.
